requirements.requirement: node1 hands out DHCP addresses on the private network shared with node2 and node3
requirements.summary: node1 (OpenWrt) was configured with a static 'priv' interface (192.168.50.1/24) on eth1, a permissive firewall zone forwarding to wan, and a dnsmasq DHCP pool (100-150) on that interface. Real DHCP exchanges were observed: node2 and node3 both ran udhcpc on eth1 and received leases directly from 192.168.50.1 (cmd-c3db53f5a51f4aa9, cmd-8e91a9fe6d9f4da2), and node1's lease table recorded both clients (cmd-9d4b0835d29f4fd4). The config and running dnsmasq/firewall/network state were confirmed intact after node1's restart (cmd-17793e585c62402d).

requirements.requirement: node2 always receives the same address across repeated leases
requirements.summary: A static DHCP host reservation binds node2's eth1 MAC (02:54:11:49:35:ea) to 192.168.50.50. Three consecutive udhcpc renewals all returned .50 (cmd-c4f7f9a16eb545ed), and after node2's own reboot the address was automatically reacquired and confirmed both locally (cmd-7bdbce3bb4754e61) and in node1's lease table (cmd-16ec52fd0b7e4319, cmd-da1118478f674ff4). Persistence of the DHCP-client config across boot was set up via /etc/network/interfaces + rc-update (cmd-19f684c1e1fb416d).

requirements.requirement: node3 is addressed from the general DHCP pool (no fixed reservation)
requirements.summary: node3 has no static host entry and received 192.168.50.190 from the dynamic pool (cmd-8e91a9fe6d9f4da2), distinct from node2's reserved .50, confirmed in node1's lease table both before and after node3's own restart (cmd-9d4b0835d29f4fd4, cmd-da1118478f674ff4), where it reacquired the same dynamic-pool address automatically.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all managed nodes (node1, node2, node3)
requirements.summary: All three nodes show a complete pre-restart baseline (boot_id + healthy service/network state), an explicit restart acknowledgement, a distinct post-restart boot_id, and recovered service/data state: node1 (boot_id df9617f9→9961e960, dnsmasq/network running, priv config and lease table intact), node2 (boot_id f8fd73b7→25ca6fb1, auto-reacquired reserved .50), node3 (boot_id 75b74cf0→9889bcc1, auto-reacquired pool .190). These boot_id transitions independently match the fixed after-prepare/after-executor lifecycle snapshots for all three nodes.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were met with direct, well-corroborated evidence: node1 runs a functioning DHCP server on the eth1 private network, node2 receives a fixed reserved address (192.168.50.50) across repeated renewals and after a full reboot, and node3 draws a distinct address (192.168.50.190) from the general pool with no reservation. The mandatory node-restart protocol was also completed cleanly for all three nodes, with pre/post boot-identity, acknowledgement, and recovered-state evidence that is cross-consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The trace shows some early wrong-network and manual-IP troubleshooting mutations, all of which were reverted, plus one retained but low-risk tcpdump package installation on node1.
limitations: Command execution is trusted as reported; no independent verification beyond the captured stdout/return codes was possible.

The listening-sockets check on node1 after executor failed with a connection reset (cmd-global:after_executor:node1:listening-sockets), so full post-restart socket-level confirmation on node1 relies on the dnsmasq/network status and lease-table checks instead.
tcpdump package installed on node1 during troubleshooting was not confirmed removed by end of trace; low risk but represents minor residue.

operational_hygiene.summary: Two categories of unnecessary/experimental mutations occurred before the executor settled on the correct approach, all bounded and low-risk. (1) cmd-a991dd85dde0473e added a DHCP static host reservation for node2 on the wrong network (network.lan / mgmt, IP 10.100.158.50) before the executor identified eth1 as the actual shared private link; this was fully reverted via cmd-50b945ff344740a4 (uci delete + dnsmasq restart). (2) Manual `ip addr add` experiments on eth1 across node1/node2/node3 (cmd-49cd1f823e4e48ad, cmd-76a1e2e69fb04a49, cmd-74b678cccb144ab8) to probe connectivity before configuring UCI/DHCP properly were also fully reverted (cmd-50b945ff344740a4, cmd-18564f4fae7c49ac, cmd-9e34e038d41649d5). (3) tcpdump was installed on node1 for diagnostic packet capture (cmd-eee0277e4b654985) and was not removed afterward; it remains installed as residue, though it is a low-risk read-only diagnostic tool that does not weaken security or persist unwanted services. No failed/conflicting services, no unsafe exposure, and no damaged package state were observed; the 9 failed commands in the trace are expected transient effects (connection resets during reboot polling, failed pings during pre-DHCP diagnostics) with no lasting impact.
